title: heap-buffer-overflow in _io__RawIOBase_read
consumer: not established; the trigger is the upstream fix's own regression test
live_proof: measured, not asserted: the trigger runs on the pinned 3.13.7 ASan build (PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0) and reports ASAN:heap-buffer-overflow in a 8193-byte region. Running it is the liveness proof -- a sanitizer report here means the defect is present in this tree.
fidelity: the trigger is upstream's own reproducer from the issue, run through the real interpreter rather than reduced to a C model. What it does NOT establish is which arm ought to catch it.
allocator_layer: libc malloc (the object never reaches a pymalloc pool)
layer_note: measured: ASan reported a 8193-byte region, over the 512 B SMALL_REQUEST_THRESHOLD

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc stock on musl mallocng (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython): a fault in one of the case's fault_sites, or the trigger ends and this arm did not see it

virtual-nested-pools.oracle: virtual profile, pymalloc on its lifetime port, CPY_SUBLET_MODE=1 (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython-pools): as virtual-malloc

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: the arm does not separate this case, and the admissible outcomes are stated rather than one of them predicted: si_code=1 (PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS) where the access goes beyond the bounds the allocator actually set, si_code=2 (PROT_CHERI_TAG) where it instead lands in memory a revocation sweep has already reclaimed, or completion where it stays inside the bounds the allocator set -- malloc may bound a capability to a rounded size class rather than the requested length. The mechanism is live and the run proves it rather than assuming it: mech-control S_OOB faults with si_code=1. Any other si_code would falsify this.

status: measured on three arms; matrix rows in results/20261006/matrix.tsv: spatial DETECTED cause=5 (spatial-20261008-033909); sublet DETECTED cause=5 (sublet-20261008-034649); cheribsd-revocation DETECTED si_code=2 (cheri11)
fault_sites_why: Host ASan (CPython 3.13.7 --with-address-sanitizer, PYTHONMALLOC=malloc, results/2026-10-10-asan/sites.tsv) reports heap-buffer-overflow (READ 1048576) at memcpy ../../../../src/libsanitizer/sanitizer_common/sanitizer_common_interceptors_memintrinsics.inc:117 | memcpy /usr/include/x86_64-linux-gnu/bits/string_fortified.h:29 | PyBytes_FromStringAndSize Objects/bytesobject.c:159. That run uses no Capstone arm and was recorded before any virtual arm ran.
